variants.name: Policy struct with function pointers (portable C)
variants.idiom_name: policy struct with a table of function pointers
variants.implementation_notes: C has no type parameterization, so the host is a struct that holds one function pointer (or a table of them) per policy axis, filled when the caller builds the host from a policy struct; a policy is therefore a set of functions with a documented signature and its state is whatever the policy struct carries. The contract lives in a header comment and is checked only by the compiler's signature checks at the assignment, so a wrong policy is a warning or a crash rather than a binding-site error. Use the C11 _Generic variant when the axis is fixed by the static type of the value being handled and no instance state is needed.
pitfalls: The policy table is mutable data: a policy struct shared by several hosts can be overwritten by one of them and silently changes every other host's behaviour.

Without _Generic (C99 and older) the type check disappears: assigning a policy function with the wrong signature is accepted or produces an unrelated warning, and the mistake surfaces as a crash inside the host.
Casts between function pointer types are not guaranteed by the standard: keep each policy signature exact and let the compiler check the assignment.

variants.name: Compile-time policy selection with _Generic
variants.idiom_name: _Generic dispatch over the static type of the argument
variants.implementation_notes: C11's _Generic chooses one of several expressions at compile time from the type of a controlling expression, which is the closest C gets to a type-bound policy: a macro selects the policy implementation for the value's static type (the mechanism behind C99's tgmath.h cbrt macro, generalised). It costs nothing at run time and needs no function pointer, but it cannot see runtime data (a pointer's dynamic type is invisible), every operation needs its own macro, and a missing association without `default` is a compile error.
variants.code_sketch:
#define cache_put(c, k, v) _Generic((k), \
    char *: cache_put_str, const char *: cache_put_str, \
    long: cache_put_int, default: cache_put_raw)((c), (k), (v))
/* resolved at compile time from the static type of (k):
   cache_put_str / cache_put_int / cache_put_raw are the policies */
pitfalls: Selection uses the static type after lvalue conversion only: a void* or a pointer whose dynamic type differs keeps the wrong policy silently.
All associations must denote expressions of the type the call site expects, and duplicate or overlapping type names in the association list are a compile error.
